title: Hawking evaporation of black holes
example_questions: What if a black hole evaporated?
How long does a black hole live?
summary: Quantum fields near a black hole horizon make it glow like a black body with a temperature inversely proportional to its mass. It slowly loses mass, gets hotter and evaporates faster, ending in a final burst. The prediction is semi-classical and widely accepted by theorists, but it has never been observed because stellar mass black holes are far colder than the cosmic microwave background.
support_note: Accepted as a robust theoretical prediction; no direct observation yet.
what_happens: The black hole radiates a faint thermal glow
Smaller means hotter, so evaporation speeds up
The final moments release the remaining mass as a burst of radiation
